### Front line

Independent mapping project DeepStateMap recorded no territorial changes for October 27. In contrast, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that forces from its "Vostok" grouping captured the settlement of Obshcheye, advancing more than five kilometers, crossing the Solonaya River, and clearing over 12 square kilometers; this claim is unverified. The Russian ministry also claimed that its artillery struck Ukrainian strongholds in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, while drone operators and snipers disrupted logistics and hit Ukrainian observation posts in the Dnipropetrovsk direction. Additionally, the Russian side claimed it halted fire and established a "regime of silence" around Oleshky in Kherson Oblast to conduct a humanitarian operation. 

According to neutral open-source monitor GeoConfirmed, a Ukrainian unit attacked a parked Russian truck with an attack drone, while Russian forces targeted claimed Ukrainian positions with FPV drones, though the outcomes were unrecorded. *The Economist* war-fire satellite model detected 28 war-related fires, mostly in Luhansk Oblast (20).

### Strikes and losses

Neutral monitor GeoConfirmed verified extensive damage to Kyiv's "Southern" railway bridge across the Dnipro River following Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile strikes, which forced city authorities to halt train services. GeoConfirmed also verified damage to the entrance and facade of the Lisova metro station, a damaged civilian vehicle, and strikes on the State University of Trade and Economics, including damage to a dormitory where 12 people were reportedly injured.

Reporting on the same events, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its overnight strikes hit Kyiv's "Southern" bridge on the grounds that it was used to transport military freight. It also claimed hits on facilities producing and storing long- and medium-range drones in Kyiv. Furthermore, the Russian ministry claimed strikes against a logistics terminal and an electronics enterprise in Kharkiv Oblast, a Ukrainian Krab self-propelled artillery system, and two cargo ships transporting military supplies to the ports of Chornomorsk and Odesa. The Russian Ministry of Defence also claimed its air defenses intercepted 222 Ukrainian drones overnight and 71 during the daytime across multiple Russian regions. 

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence claimed that Ukrainian drones have killed or wounded 302,000 Russian soldiers since the beginning of 2026, including 27,829 between October 1 and October 25, asserting that each strike was verified on video.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence announced that domestic defense enterprises have secured 54 preferential leasing agreements worth 244.53 million hryvnias, and that its procurement agency received an international ISO anti-bribery certificate. The ministry also reported that the Ukrainian parliament passed legislation extending residence permit deadlines for foreign contract soldiers, while officials advanced legal preparations for the NATO Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA). Bilaterally, Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara met with Moldovan Defense Minister Anatolie Nosatîi to discuss air defense and counter-drone cooperation.

The Russian Ministry of Defence stated that Defense Minister Andrei Belousov inspected the command post of the "Dnepr" troop grouping, ordering personnel to boost the effectiveness of strike drones. Russian defense officials also reported holding bilateral military cooperation talks with delegations from Mali and Madagascar.
